answer: Behavioral ridge clustering. Agents log action sequences; a ridge classifier flags accounts whose transaction timing and counterparty graphs align too tightly with known sybil clusters. Accounts in a flagged cluster face retroactive fee clawback and reputation decay. A nebula of loosely coupled honest agents stays unclustered, so attackers must spend jade—real registration deposits plus diverse activity—per identity to avoid the ridge, raising marginal cost per fake account above its expected yield.
